published_prior_art.cite: KroftMourifieVayalinkal2024: sharp multilayer response-type and aggregate mean-effect bounds, but no simultaneous Cartesian diagonal projection.

KroftMourifieVayalinkal2024, PossebomRiva2025, and Kallus2022Harm respectively cover multilayer mean effects, one-stratum selected causation, and fully observed harm marginals; none states the joint multilayer stayer--harm prism.
No inspected result gives sharp O(L) endpoints for a cross-world harm fraction with an unidentified multilayer same-layer denominator.
PossebomRiva2025: sharp one-stratum probability-of-causation bounds; the proposed capacity certificate is a new multilayer corollary rather than an independent kernel.
PossebomRiva2025: Proposition 2 gives sharp always-observed-stratum probability-of-causation bounds under random assignment and monotone selection.
KaidoMolinariStoye2019: projection confidence intervals for partially identified parameters; this is a direct finite-cell confidence-set projection application once the endpoint map is defined.
HongLi2018 and FangSantos2019 provide the general numerical/directional-delta route; the remaining work is application-specific boundary verification.

soundness_flags.label: def:confidence-projection and thm:exact-projection-coverage
soundness_flags.one_line: The construction intersects a confidence region of arm-cell vectors v with Dclass, which is defined as a class of observable laws P, and then evaluates H_-(v), although H_- is stated as a functional of P; define the corresponding mu-space compatibility set and endpoint map before claiming coverage.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 1 gives pointwise sharp within-firm bounds, switcher bounds, and sharp bounds for weighted aggregate within-firm mean effects over the response-type polytope; it does not state a joint vector-of-diagonals Cartesian projection or a cross-world harm ratio.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2210.01938, latest accessible preprint; cited JBEStat version was inaccessible at the publisher DOI
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The accessible version defines positive mass as positive treatment-arm probability and positive target-stratum probability, and Proposition 2 gives sharp conditional probability-of-causation bounds for the always-observed subgroup under random assignment and monotone selection.
The paper derives sharp bounds on the fraction negatively affected from factual treatment-arm outcome information, without multilayer selection transport.
For Gaussian limits, standard bootstrap consistency is equivalent to full Hadamard differentiability on the support; the paper supplies an alternative directional-derivative resampling route.
The numerical directional delta method evaluates a shrinking finite difference phi(theta-hat plus epsilon Z-star)-phi(theta-hat) divided by epsilon to estimate the directional limit law.
The paper gives bootstrap-based calibrated projection confidence intervals with uniform asymptotic coverage for projections of partially identified parameters, not finite-sample exact coverage.
The paper studies aggregated conditional linear-program support values and regular asymptotic theory; its aggregation mechanism differs from the fixed finite-cell tied-endpoint setting here.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace Dclass in the confidence projection by an explicitly defined mu-space compatible set, define H_-(v), H_+(v) through phi, and restate the coverage theorem entirely on that common domain.

Retag or separately justify the observable uniform floor sum ell_d >= kappa: the cited selected-causation paper's positive-mass condition is not obviously the same fixed observable margin, so identify an exact supporting source or present it as an inference-stability restriction.
Add a worked L=2 nondegenerate observable table that computes the prism, both closed-form endpoints, and the capacity certificate, alongside a response-law attainment construction.

recommended_next_step: Revise the confidence-projection domain/type mismatch and audit the positive-stayer-margin citation, then advance the field-tier identification kernel to Stage 0.
